news.headline: Apple WWDC Keynote Kicks Off Monday; AAPL Near Record as Siri AI Overhaul Eyed
news.body: Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference opened June 8 with Wall Street watching closely for a revamped Siri powered by Gemini AI and broader Apple Intelligence updates—what Morgan Stanley called the year's key catalyst for the stock. AAPL climbed roughly 15% in May and entered the event near record highs after a string of analyst target upgrades, with Wedbush setting a Street-high $400 price target. Bank of America projects $15–$30 billion in AI-related revenue by fiscal 2030 from an Apple AI pivot. A disappointing keynote could trigger a sharp reversal in a stock already priced for strong AI credibility, making the event a binary risk for the broader Nasdaq.

news.headline: SpaceX IPO Roadshow Active; $75B Raise at $135/Share Targets June 12 Nasdaq Debut
news.body: SpaceX's roadshow, which kicked off June 4 after an accelerated SEC review, is targeting a $75 billion raise at $135 per share, implying a $1.77 trillion valuation and what would be the largest IPO in history. The offering would make SpaceX the seventh-largest U.S. company by market cap, surpassing Tesla. Musk retains over 82% voting control post-offering, and Goldman Sachs leads the underwriting syndicate. Market participants are watching for demand signals ahead of June 11 pricing and June 12 trading debut under ticker SPCX on Nasdaq.

news.headline: Iran Missiles Hit Israel, Shattering Ceasefire; Dow Futures Drop 199 Pts
news.body: Iran launched ballistic missiles at Israel on June 7-8, 2026, its first direct attack since April's ceasefire, prompting retaliatory Israeli airstrikes on western and central Iran. Dow futures fell as much as 199 points in overnight trading while WTI crude surged over 3% to $93.45 and Brent jumped 3.6% to $96.47, amplifying fears of sustained oil supply disruption. The geopolitical shock compounds last week's Nasdaq selloff, raising Fed-rate and energy-cost concerns simultaneously for U.S. equities. Asian markets dropped sharply, with South Korea's Kospi plunging over 8% before paring losses, setting a risk-off tone for Monday's Wall Street open.

news.headline: Meta Shares Sink 7% on Report of Tens-of-Billions AI Stock Offering
news.body: Meta Platforms fell as much as 7% on June 5 after the Financial Times reported the social media giant is weighing a multi-billion-dollar equity raise to fund AI infrastructure, following rival Alphabet's record $85 billion share sale. Meta has already raised its 2026 capex guidance to a range of $125–$145 billion, nearly double its prior-year spending, sparking dilution fears among shareholders. Reports then emerged that Microsoft and Amazon are exploring similar equity raises, turning the story into a sector-wide capital-market overhang for hyperscaler stocks. The AI arms-race fundraising wave is pressuring megacap valuations across the Nasdaq and S&P 500, with markets questioning whether public equity can absorb the wave of new issuance.

news.headline: Healthcare Stocks Lead S&P Rotation; UNH, Eli Lilly Surge as Investors Flee Tech
news.body: The S&P 500 Healthcare sector surged 3% on June 5 as investors rotated out of battered chip and AI names into defensive and growth healthcare plays, with UnitedHealth Group and Eli Lilly leading the charge. Bank of America upgraded UnitedHealth to Buy, citing improving cost trends and a favorable earnings outlook, sending UNH shares up more than 5%; Eli Lilly added 4% and extended gains after CVS Health agreed to cover Lilly's new weight-loss pill Foundayo. The Health Care SPDR ETF (XLV) broke above a key short-term resistance level on elevated institutional volume, signaling a potential leadership rotation that markets are watching heading into the week. The divergence between healthcare's outperformance and technology's selloff highlights a broad sector re-rating as investors reassess stretched AI valuations.

news.headline: KOSPI Triggers Circuit Breaker, Plunges 8%+ as Samsung & SK Hynix Crash on AI Fears
news.body: South Korea's KOSPI cratered more than 8.37% at the open on June 8, triggering a 20-minute emergency circuit breaker — the third such halt of 2026. Samsung Electronics fell as much as 11% below the 300,000 won mark and SK Hynix slid roughly 10%, with the two stocks together accounting for ~50% of the index's market cap. The selloff was driven by compounding pressures: Broadcom's below-consensus AI chip guidance (Q3 target of $16B vs. $17.2B expected), Iran missile strikes on Israel reigniting geopolitical risk, a stronger-than-expected US payrolls print fuelling Fed rate-hike fears, and margin-call cascades from record retail leverage of 37.74 trillion won. South Korean financial authorities issued an emergency statement pledging intervention; the won fell to near 1,560 per dollar.

news.headline: Nikkei 225 Drops ~4% Intraday as SoftBank, Tokyo Electron Lead Japan Tech Rout
news.body: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell nearly 4% intraday on June 8, sliding to a low of 63,987 before partially recovering, extending losses from Friday's 1.31% decline. SoftBank Group plunged 7.5% and Tokyo Electron dropped 6.7%, with Advantest off 5%, as the Broadcom AI guidance miss and renewed Iran-Israel hostilities hit high-multiple AI proxy names hardest. The dollar-yen approached the 160 intervention warning level at 159.953, adding pressure on rate-sensitive equities. Bloomberg reported the Bank of Japan is likely to discuss raising its policy rate from 0.75% to 1.0% at its June 16 meeting, adding a dual headwind of tighter monetary policy to the tech-sector selloff.

news.headline: Hang Seng Slides to Lowest Since March as Iran-Israel Strikes Amplify Tech Retreat
news.body: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 437 points, or 1.5%, to 24,585 on June 8, hitting its lowest level since March 2026 and extending a four-session losing streak. The decline was driven by a broad retreat in AI and technology stocks following the global semiconductor selloff, compounded by reports that Iran fired missiles at Israel on June 7, testing a fragile ceasefire and lifting oil prices. SMIC dropped 7.2% and Lenovo fell 5.1% among the biggest drags; AIA Group also slid 1.0% amid concerns over mainland China capital-control risks. The CSI 300 was simultaneously under pressure, down 1.6% on June 7, reflecting the same risk-off confluence.

news.headline: BOJ Said to Mull June 16 Rate Hike to 1%, Adding Policy Pressure on Japanese Equities
news.body: Bloomberg reported on June 4–5 that Bank of Japan officials are actively considering raising the policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.0% at the June 16 Monetary Policy Meeting, with scope for further hikes later in 2026. Officials cited persistently low real interest rates and upside inflation risks tied to oil prices from the Iran conflict as key drivers. Japan's real wages rose for a fourth consecutive month, strengthening the tightening case. The prospect of a BoJ hike amid a weak yen (approaching 160) and a tech-sector selloff has compounded headwinds for the Nikkei 225, which had rallied ~32% year-to-date to record highs.

news.headline: KOSPI Sidecar Triggered on June 5 as Broadcom Guidance Miss Sparks Asian Chip Rout
news.body: On June 5, the KOSPI slumped 5.54% to 8,160.59, with a sidecar circuit breaker activated after KOSPI 200 futures fell 5%, following Broadcom's Q3 AI chip revenue guidance of $16B — approximately 7% below the $17.2B consensus. SK Hynix plunged 9.92%, wiping nearly $100B in market value in a single session, while Samsung Electronics fell 6.4%; Tokyo Electron and Advantest dropped 6.7% and 5% in Japan. Foreign investors net-sold approximately $22B in Korean stocks since May, with the Korean won hitting its lowest since 2009. Goldman Sachs analysts noted the selling was driven by crowded-position liquidation rather than deteriorating fundamentals.

news.headline: Brent Surges 4%+ as Iran-Israel Missile Exchange Threatens Ceasefire Collapse
news.body: Brent crude futures jumped more than 4% to above $97/bbl on Monday June 8, rebounding sharply after Iran launched multiple ballistic missiles at Israel—the first direct attack since the April ceasefire—and Israel subsequently struck targets in western and central Iran. The continued near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which has disrupted roughly 20% of global oil supply, kept the underlying bid firm despite OPEC+ approving an additional 188,000 b/d increase in July production quotas. Markets are now reassessing whether the U.S.-brokered 60-day truce framework can survive, with any full ceasefire breakdown seen as a major upside price catalyst. Brent had shed ~3% on Friday on weak China demand data before this sharp reversal.

news.headline: Gold Hits 2026 Low Near $4,370 as NFP Shock Sends Fed Rate-Hike Odds to 98%
news.body: Spot gold fell below $4,370/oz on Friday June 6—its lowest level since March 2026 and down nearly 4% on the week—after May nonfarm payrolls printed at 172,000, more than double the 85,000 consensus, with April revised up to 179,000. The data triggered an immediate repricing in Fed policy, with market-implied rate-hike probability surging to 98% by year-end; the 10-year Treasury yield jumped 8 bps to 4.53% and the DXY hit its strongest level since early April. Gold has now erased all its 2026 gains and sits roughly 18% below pre-war highs, as the combination of elevated oil-driven inflation and a resilient labor market leaves the Fed no room to ease. Cleveland Fed President Hammack signaled rates should remain steady for now but flagged possible hikes if trends continue.

news.headline: Thermal Coal Hits 19-Month High Above $148/T on China Mine Explosion, Safety Crackdown
news.body: Thermal coal futures surged above $145/T—their highest since October 2024, up ~10% over four weeks—after a deadly gas explosion at an illegal-labor mine in China's Shanxi province triggered province-wide safety inspections and production suspensions across the country's largest coal-producing region. The Shanxi incident, described as China's worst coal mine disaster in 17 years with 82 fatalities, is expected to materially constrain near-term Chinese thermal and coking coal output, threatening power security ahead of summer demand. Australian coking coal simultaneously approached February's 20-month high at ~$241/T as buyers sought alternatives to disrupted Chinese supply. Elevated LNG prices from the Strait of Hormuz closure further increased coal's relative cost advantage, adding demand-side support.

news.headline: Copper Retreats to ~$6.30/lb as Chile Posts Weakest April Output in 23 Years
news.body: Copper futures pulled back toward $6.30/lb on Friday, retreating from record highs, as Chile's April 2026 copper production fell 13.8% year-on-year to just 399,954 metric tons—its weakest April reading in 23 years—driven by declining ore grades and high comparison bases at major producers including BHP's Escondida and Codelco. The supply-side weakness was offset by deteriorating demand expectations: rising Fed rate-hike bets, slowing Chinese growth, and the Strait of Hormuz disruption dampening industrial activity. Pending U.S. tariff decisions on copper imports have encouraged front-loaded shipments into U.S. ports, distorting near-term physical balances. Cochilco raised its 2026 price forecast to $4.95/lb citing structural supply tightness, while Q1 Chilean output declined 5.8% overall.

news.headline: UK Natural Gas Rebounds Above 117p/Therm as Europe Storage Sits at Just 38% Full
news.body: UK NBP natural gas futures recovered above 117 pence per therm on June 6-7, bouncing from a three-week low, as the Strait of Hormuz remained at near-standstill traffic levels disrupting roughly one-fifth of global LNG supplies and complicating European efforts to rebuild inventories ahead of winter. European storage currently stands at only 38% capacity—critically low for this time of year—while the UK nuclear fleet remains heavily constrained with four reactors offline, sustaining elevated gas-for-power demand. Iran and Israel trading fresh missile strikes over the weekend raised fresh doubts about the diplomatic path to a Hormuz reopening, keeping winter-contract premiums elevated. UK household energy bills are set to rise 13% under the July 2026 price cap as wholesale price pressures feed through.
